# Ghosts Old Content Audit

This manifest audits the read-only recovery source at
`Ghosts_old/MMOCoreORB/bin/scripts` against the current server at
`MMOCoreORB/bin/scripts`.

The detailed appendix is mechanically generated from SHA-256 comparisons so
that every old file receives a disposition. Classifications marked
`MANUAL_REVIEW_REQUIRED` are audit work items, not approval to copy the file.
They are promoted to a final migration classification only after their
registration and dependency chains have been inspected.

## Safety boundaries

- `Ghosts_old` is read-only.
- Current Core3/Engine3/C++ and build sources are authoritative and excluded.
- SQL, databases, backups, accounts, characters, inventories, and runtime
  persistence are excluded.
- Current Jedi discovery and rank progression are authoritative.
- Obsolete Flurry/custom convenience terminals are not migration candidates.
- Normal travel infrastructure is retained and repaired.

## Required repair findings

## Inventory reconciliation

- Old files inventoried: **50,850** (295 MiB).
- Current files inventoried: **44,767**.
- Identical at the same path: **26,100**.
- Identical content already present at a different path: **236**.
- Same-path files where the current implementation differs and remains
  authoritative: **12,512**.
- Old IFF/client assets requiring an existing TRE/client dependency: **179**.
- Generated/archive/legacy terminal/legacy AI files excluded: **63**.
- Remaining unique old content is retained in the per-file ledger as an
  explicit review item until its complete registration chain is proven. It is
  not silently omitted and is not safe to bulk-copy.

No C++, build source, SQL, database backup, account, character, inventory, or
persisted-world data was migrated.

### Jedi trainer type resolution

The current supported trainer flow is `trainerConvHandler` -> `SkillTrainer`
-> `LuaSkillManager`. Advanced Jedi trainers have explicit trainer tables, but
the type resolver could replace an explicit Grand Jedi Master or Dark Jedi
Lord type with the generic `trainer_jedi` type when the NPC matched a player's
generated Jedi-trainer coordinates. The current repair gives explicit advanced
trainer types precedence while retaining all normal prerequisite, XP,
skill-point, credit, and progression checks.

### Trainer visible names

The two spawned advanced trainers mixed a generic Jedi STF name, generated
random-name tagging, and a custom title. They now use unambiguous custom names:
`Grand Jedi Master Trainer` and `Dark Jedi Lord Trainer`.

### Flurry and travel separation

`object/tangible/terminal/terminal_travel.iff` remains the normal travel
terminal with game object type `16402`. The medical replacement is a
`surgical_droid_21b` mobile with its own radial component. The obsolete Flurry
screenplay is not included at startup and is not assigned to travel templates.
Three residual `beta_terminal_wound.iff` scene spawns (two on Kaas and one on
Geonosis) were removed. These were legacy wound/buff-terminal objects, not
travel terminals. Normal `terminal_travel.iff`, ticket collectors, shuttleports,
starports, travel-point definitions, and native travel handling were retained.

## Custom planet discovery

The old/current content contains these non-stock or expansion/custom ground
zones: **Chandrila, Coruscant, Concord Dawn, Concordia, Geonosis, Hoth, Hutta
(old name: Nal Hutta), Jakku, Kaas, Kashyyyk, Korriban, Mandalore, Mustafar,
and Taanab**. Current `config.lua` deliberately has every one of these zones
disabled; the enabled ground set is Corellia, Dantooine, Dathomir, Endor, Lok,
Naboo, Rori, Talus, Tatooine, Tutorial, and Yavin 4. Content presence is not
equivalent to a safely enabled zone: terrain/TRE, travel, region, mobile, loot,
and screenplay chains must all validate first.

Current planet-manager travel definitions exist for Coruscant, Chandrila,
Geonosis, Concordia, Concord Dawn, Hoth, Hutta, Jakku, Kaas, Kashyyyk,
Korriban, Mandalore, Mustafar, and Taanab. Current city travel-terminal
screenplays exist for Coruscant, Geonosis, Hoth, Hutta, Jakku, Kaas, Korriban,
Mandalore, and Taanab. Missing old `NalHuttaHuttCityScreenPlay` is superseded
by the current `HuttaCityScreenPlay`; old Bela Vistal, Vreni Island, and Nym
Stronghold registrations are likewise superseded by the current CityScreenPlay
implementations rather than copied under duplicate names.

## Validation findings

A repository-wide Lua parse pass found ten syntactically invalid current files.
One reachable custom-planet mobile,
`mobile/korriban/creatures/mutated_rancor_sith.lua`, had a prematurely closed
loot table and a missing separator; it was repaired and now parses. The other
nine are dormant database-migration, unfinished/copy, unregistered screenplay,
disabled world-boss, or unregistered object-source files and are recorded as
blockers rather than being silently activated or broadly rewritten.

## 2026-08-29 focused repair pass

- **Custom planet configuration root cause:** current Core3 reads
  `scripts/managers/planet/planet_manager.lua`; the custom tables were in the
  unused legacy path `scripts/managers/planet_manager.lua`.  Valid current
  tables were added for Coruscant, Geonosis, Hoth, Hutta, Jakku, Kaas,
  Kashyyyk, Korriban, Mandalore, Mustafar, Taanab and Dungeon2.
- **Custom planet region root cause:** current Core3 loads
  `scripts/managers/planet/<zone>_regions.lua`; the custom region files were in
  `scripts/managers/spawn_manager`.  Current-path region files were created and
  validated with `luac`.
- **Custom planet resources:** the resource manager's `activeZones` list was
  stock-only.  The eleven custom playable planets were added without changing
  resource classes or statistics.
- **Survey Tool root cause:** `survey_tool_all.lua` was registered without
  `templateType = SURVEYTOOL`, so `SurveyToolImplementation` rejected it.  It
  now uses the current SurveyTool template contract as the starter organic
  tool.  A single truly universal organic/inorganic tool is not supported by
  current content fields and would require C++.
- **Custom travel root cause:** custom city scripts placed purchase terminals
  but no `player_transport` with `ShuttleZoneComponent`; consequently travel
  points had no scheduled shuttle and destinations were rejected.  A dedicated
  screenplay now supplies the missing collectors and native shuttle objects.
- **Medical Droid visibility root cause:** the droid used one custom buff CRC
  with no client presentation entry.  It now calls the existing nine-stat
  medical service path, preserving +2200 for 7200 seconds while using the
  client-recognized medical/performance buff CRCs.
- **Jedi powers while armored:** the rejection is hard-coded in current C++
  command headers and `QueueCommand.cpp`; no content/config override exists.
  Status: `REQUIRES_C++_NOT_IMPLEMENTED` under this pass's no-C++ rule.
- **World bosses:** templates, five corrupted-boss mobiles, `worldbosscrate`
  loot, and spawn-point data were already present.  The current rotating boss
  screenplay was dormant; it is now registered after repairing an undefined
  minimum distance, a zero-based random index, and undefined fallback/event
  values.  The overlapping legacy Flurry spawner remains dormant to prevent
  duplicate populations.
- **Runtime validation blocker:** a separate live Core3/ORB owner was already
  bound to port 44419.  The duplicate verification process was stopped; these
  changes require a clean restart of the live server before in-game validation.
